title: Chemically Meaningful Textualization Enables Explainable Validation of Metal-Organic Frameworks by Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.11283v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Computation-ready metal-organic framework (MOF) databases are essential for high-throughput screening, yet many reported crystal structures remain chemically unreasonable or disordered, compromising simulation fidelity. Existing validation approaches can identify non-computation-ready structures, but they often rely on heuristic rules, license requirement, or offer limited interpretability. Here, we show that large language models (LLMs) can serve as interpretable validators of MOF structures when crystallographic information is transformed into chemically meaningful text. By benchmarking nine descriptors, we find that successful LLM-based validation depends not on the amount of structural information alone, but on whether local coordination, framework connectivity, and chemical context are organized into a linguistically learnable representation. translated_title: 化学有意义的文本化使大型语言模型能够对金属有机框架进行可解释的验证
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11283v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：计算就绪的金属有机框架（MOF）数据库对于高通量筛选至关重要，然而许多报道的晶体结构在化学上不合理或存在无序性，这损害了模拟的保真度。现有的验证方法能够识别非计算就绪的结构，但它们往往依赖启发式规则、许可证要求，或提供有限的可解释性。在此，我们表明，当晶体学信息被转化为化学有意义的文本时，大型语言模型（LLMs）可以作为MOF结构的可解释验证器。通过基准测试九种描述符，我们发现基于LLM的成功验证不仅依赖于结构信息的数量，还取决于局部配位、框架连通性和化学环境是否被组织成一种语言上可学习的形式。使用专门描述符（mof2text）微调的LLM实现了与现有方法相当的性能。
tldr: 本文证明，将MOF晶体结构转化为化学有意义的文本表示（如mof2text描述符）后，大型语言模型能够以可解释且性能可比的方式验证金属有机框架结构的化学合理性，其成功关键在于局部配位和框架连通性的语言化组织而非单纯的信息量。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that transforming MOF crystal structures into chemically meaningful textual representations (e.g., mof2text descriptors) enables large language models to validate metal-organic framework structures with interpretability and comparable performance, where success depends on linguistically organized local coordination and connectivity rather than raw information volume.
